editorial:
Imagine spending your whole summer just hanging out, drinking, and smoking with your best buds. That is exactly where you find Jack. He seems like just another lazy guy in the crowd, but he has a secret spark. While his friends are happy doing nothing, you can tell Jack is itching for something more. He wants to be a real writer. The movie captures that weird feeling of being young and stuck in a rut, but still having big dreams for the future. It feels like a slow own-your-life journey where the vibe is mostly relaxed and hazy, just like a long summer break that never seems to end.

What really works here is how natural the friendships feel. You will recognize the group dynamics and the way they push each other. The pacing is a bit slow, which might bother some, but it fits the mood perfectly. If you enjoy stories about finding yourself and figuring out your passion, you should definitely give this one a shot. Since it is an older film, you will want to look for the best version available. I suggest adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection to get the best picture quality, or check if you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch.
endingExplained: After a summer of idling around, Jack finally finds the spark he needs for his book. He realizes that the people and the boring moments around him are actually his best material. The movie ends with him finally committing to his writing instead of just talking about it. He moves away from the lazy habits of his friends to chase his dream, showing that he has finally grown up and found his purpose in life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about young people finding their way in life.
